deep.reconstruction:
Context: Chapter VI of the Tractatus de numerorum doctrina studies the residues mod d of the arithmetic progression a, a+b, a+2b, ... (term with index i is a+(i-1)b). Section 171 split the problem into two cases, gcd(b,d)=1 and gcd(b,d)>1. This page treats the coprime case.

§172. Assume gcd(b,d)=1. Claim: the first residue (that of a) does not return before the term a+db. Proof: suppose a+(d-n)b ≡ a (mod d) with 0<n<d. Then d | (d-n)b, hence d | nb. Since gcd(b,d)=1, d | n, which is impossible for 0<n<d. (Euler cites no lemma for the step from d | nb to d | n; it is Euclid's lemma / Euclid VII.30 generalized.)

§173. So it suffices to consider the d terms a+nb for n=0,...,d-1. Call their residues α, β, γ, δ, ε, ..., λ.

§174. Claim: these d residues are pairwise distinct. Euler argues explicitly only for β, the residue of a+b. If a+nb ≡ a+b with 1<n<d, then d | (n-1)b, so d | (n-1) with 0<n-1<d, a contradiction. The general case a+ib ≡ a+jb with 0≤i<j<d gives d | (j-i)b and the same contradiction; this is implied by 'ita etiam', but the generalization is mine.

§175. There are d distinct residues, all lying in {0,1,...,d-1}, a set of d elements. Hence every element occurs: {a+nb mod d : 0≤n<d} is a complete residue system (pigeonhole).

§176. Therefore for every r with 0≤r<d there is n<d with a+nb ≡ r (mod d). In particular, for r=0 some term is divisible by d.

§177. Restated: for any integer c (=a-r) and gcd(b,d)=1 there is n<d with d | c+nb. This is the solvability of the linear congruence bn ≡ -c (mod d).

§178. Let a+mb ≡ 0 (mod d) with m<d. Then a+(m+1)b ≡ b and a+(m-1)b ≡ -b ≡ d-b. Let a+nb ≡ 1. Subtracting the first congruence from this one gives (n-m)b ≡ 1.

§179. Put p=n-m, so pb ≡ 1 (mod d); p is an inverse of b mod d. Then a+(m+kp)b ≡ k (mod d) for k=1,2,3,..., and in general.

§180. If m+kp ≥ d, reduce it mod d to an index k'<d. The term a+k'b still leaves residue k.

§181. A simpler route once p (with pb ≡ 1) is known: a ≡ α implies a+npb ≡ α+n (mod d).

§182. To obtain a prescribed residue r, set n=r-α. The required term is a+(r-α)pb, or in general a+((r-α)p ± μd)b, with μ chosen so that the index lies in [0,d).

Next page (§183): this reduces to finding p, q with pb - qd = 1, i.e. the Bezout identity / Euclidean algorithm. In short, the page proves that n ↦ a+nb permutes Z/dZ when gcd(b,d)=1. It then solves the linear congruence a+nb ≡ r via the modular inverse of b: n ≡ (r-α)b^{-1} (mod d).
errors: §174 explicitly treats only the second residue β; the general distinctness of the residues of a+ib and a+jb is asserted by analogy ('ita etiam'), not written out. The gap is trivial.
§178: 'terminus sequens a+(m+1)b residuum dabit b' and 'praecedens ... residuum -b, seu d-b' are literally correct only if 0<b<d. In general the residues are b mod d and -b mod d.
§178–179: p=n-m may be negative (if n<m); it must then be reduced mod d (p+d). Euler does not remark on this.
§179: 'termino a+(m+np)b residuum = n' holds as a least residue only for n<d; otherwise it is n mod d. The letter n is also reused with a different meaning from §178.
§181: the residue α+n must be reduced mod d when α+n ≥ d.
§182: the condition (r-α)p ± μd < d should also require nonnegativity (0 ≤ ... < d), since r-α can be negative. This is a minor omission.

results.what: If gcd(b,d)=1, the first d terms a+nb (0≤n<d) of an arithmetic progression have pairwise distinct residues mod d. Hence they form a complete residue system (the affine map n ↦ a+bn is a bijection of Z/dZ).
results.modern_name: Complete residue system under multiplication by a unit / affine permutation of Z/dZ
results.usually_credited_to: Implicit in Bachet (1621) and earlier Indian kuttaka work; systematized by Gauss, Disquisitiones Arithmeticae (1801), arts. 23–24

results.what: Solvability of a+nb ≡ r (mod d) for every r when gcd(b,d)=1, with a solution n<d.
results.modern_name: Solvability of the linear congruence bx ≡ c (mod d)
results.usually_credited_to: Aryabhata/Brahmagupta (kuttaka), Bachet 1621; Gauss 1801 for congruence formalism

results.what: Construction of the solution via p with pb ≡ 1 (mod d): the term with residue r is a+((r-α)p mod d)b.
results.modern_name: Solving linear congruences via the modular inverse

results.what: The period of residues of a+nb mod d is exactly d when gcd(b,d)=1.
results.modern_name: Order of b in the additive group Z/dZ equals d/gcd(b,d)
results.usually_credited_to: folklore; Euler's own published papers (e.g. E262, 1761) use it

deep.surprise_reason: This is standard elementary material: complete residue systems and solving linear congruences with a modular inverse. It is well known to appear in Euler's Tractatus de numerorum doctrina, published in 1849 in the Opera postuma and in Opera Omnia I.5. Its interest is pedagogical and historical, as a pre-Gaussian treatment without congruence notation, not as a new result.

checkable.asserts: §173–175: for gcd(b,d)=1 the residues of a+nb, n=0..d-1, are exactly 0..d-1.

checkable.sympy: all(min([k for k in range(1, 2*d+1) if (k*b) % d == 0]) == d for d in range(2, 40) for b in range(1, 40) if gcd(b, d) == 1)
checkable.asserts: §172: the residue of a first recurs at index shift exactly d (term a+db) when gcd(b,d)=1.

checkable.sympy: all((a + (((r - a % d) * mod_inverse(b, d)) % d) * b) % d == r for d in range(2, 25) for b in range(1, 25) for a in range(0, 25) for r in range(d) if gcd(b, d) == 1)
checkable.asserts: §181–182: with p = b^{-1} mod d and α = a mod d, the term a + ((r-α)p mod d) b leaves residue r.

checkable.sympy: all((a + (m + k*p)*b) % d == k % d for d in [7, 11, 12, 15] for b in [1, 5, 7] for a in [0, 3, 10] if gcd(b, d) == 1 for p in [mod_inverse(b, d)] for m in [((-a) * p) % d] for k in range(0, 3*d))
checkable.asserts: §178–180: if a+mb ≡ 0 and pb ≡ 1 (mod d), then a+(m+kp)b ≡ k (mod d).
Worked example of §182: d=7, b=3, a=5 (α=5), p=5; the term with residue 2 is a+6b = 23 ≡ 2 (mod 7).
